nodes.title: At the table
nodes.body:
The tart is still on the table when the lamps burn down.

Serenity takes one slice upstairs, wrapped in a napkin. She doesn't say why. The other stays under the cloth, where Ambrose will find it in the morning and know exactly what had and hadn't happened.

I don't write *forgiveness* in my margin. Nobody said it. I'm not going to put a word in a place it hasn't been earned.

I write down his answer instead. It's short. It's accurate. It's the best thing he's said all month.
nodes.braidText: At the Kitchens table, Wicker answered Serenity's question. Nobody forgave anybody. She took one slice of tart upstairs.

castMemories.memory: Serenity took one slice of Ambrose's pear tart upstairs after her talk with Wicker, and left the other under the cloth.

nodes.title: A greenhouse evening
nodes.body:
Serenity takes the path behind the greenhouses on her own.

It's a clear cold evening, with the first frost beginning in the grass. The glass houses stand in a row against a violet sky, lit from within like paper lanterns, and each of them breathes out a faint green warmth as she goes by. Soren's bird is in one coat pocket. The map case bumps her hip. She's left a note on the Kitchen table that says only *Out.* Neither of them gets a say tonight.

The little greenhouse is the last in the row. It's the oldest, and the smallest, and it's still warm from the day. There's a smell of tomato leaves and wet clay and the sweetness of a single late geranium, and a faint ticking where the sun's heat's leaving the iron. There are two chairs. A moth's asleep on the watering can, a big soft grey one with feathery antennae, its wings folded like a closed book.

She sits beside it and takes out a card.

On one side she draws the pantry door, green, with the little brass latch. On the other, the path that brought her here, a thin pencilled line through the grass. Somewhere nobody else can hear, in the stone beyond the glass, a page turns.

She lets it.

She doesn't tilt her head. She doesn't hold her breath. She just lets it turn, as you'd let a clock tick, and goes on drawing.

Penny stops outside with two paper cups. She doesn't come in. She stands in the doorway of the greenhouse, in the cold, with the steam from the cups going up past her glasses.

“I can leave one,” she says. “Or both.”

Serenity opens the door a crack, and looks at her.

“You've got exactly one minute to tell me if the Vault notices are still arguing.”

“Seven minutes. Permancer used a colon.”

Serenity laughs. It's a real laugh, short and delighted, and the moth moves one antenna in its sleep. She takes a cup. Penny stays on the step.

Serenity looks at the second chair. Then at the dark path home, running away through the frost to the lit windows of the Academy.

I want to keep one of them.

choices.title: Penny in the second chair.
choices.result:
“You can stay,” Serenity says. “No more colons.”

Penny sits. She does it carefully, as if the second chair might change its mind. They spend the next hour giving the moth terrible names, each worse than the last: Sir Fluffington, the Dowager Grey, Mister Soft Landing. The moth sleeps through all of them.
choices.braidText: Serenity let Penny into the greenhouse. They spent an hour giving a sleeping moth terrible names.

castMemories.memory: Serenity let Penny into the greenhouse, and they spent an hour giving a sleeping moth terrible names.
castMemories.aside: Penny and I named a moth. Sir Fluffington was hers. I'd like that on the record.

choices.title: The walk home alone.
choices.result:
“Take the other cup to Ambrose,” Serenity says.

Penny nods, once, and goes, without a word of argument, which is the kindest thing she could've done. Serenity finishes drawing the path on the back of the card. She gives it an arrow at the end, pointing home, and a very small boat, with a flag.
choices.braidText: Serenity sent Penny back with the other cup and walked home alone. She drew the path on a card, with an arrow pointing home.

castMemories.memory: Serenity sent Penny back with the other cup and walked home alone, drawing the path on a card with an arrow pointing home.
castMemories.aside: I walked home alone. On purpose. I drew the path with an arrow, in case I forgot which way.

castMemories.memory: Serenity spent an evening in the little greenhouse with a sleeping moth, and let a far-off page turn without listening for it.
castMemories.aside: I let the page turn and didn't listen. It's harder than it sounds. The moth was very good at it.

nodes.title: A greenhouse evening
nodes.body:
The moth hasn't moved.

Serenity shuts the greenhouse door gently, so it can keep sleeping. The latch makes the smallest click you've ever heard.

I'm not giving her evening a name. She didn't give it one. It was hers, and that's all I'm going to write on it.
nodes.braidText: Serenity spent an evening in the little greenhouse with a sleeping moth. It was hers.

storyScenes.title: The Turned-Down Place Card
storyScenes.opening:
Ambrose kept the Count's place card.

His name is on the front, in the neat black capitals of a man who writes place cards for people who aren't coming. On the back, there's a small round ring where the soup bowl stood, pale gold, a little greasy at the edge.

When the table was cleared, Ambrose picked it up. He looked at it for a while. Then he turned it over, name-side down, and propped it against the salt, the way you'd turn down a photograph in a room where someone's left.

I've kept it like that.

storyScenes.title: The Two-Sided Bookmark
storyScenes.opening:
The Vault made this from the brass that ran round the old doorway.

It's a narrow bar, no longer than a finger, with the weight of a coin. IN is stamped at one end. OUT is stamped at the other. Penny checked both. She checked the letters, and the edges, and the way it caught the light. Then she checked what happened when she turned it over.

It said the same thing. That was the thing that pleased her.

storyScenes.title: The Paper Fold
storyScenes.opening:
One fold stayed out when the room went home.

It's a small flap of cream paper, no bigger than a playing card. There's a corner of window on it, a little pencilled square of unwritten night, and a thumb mark where Wicker waited. It's a clean oval, a little darker at the edge, the exact shape of a held breath.

Hold it up to the light. The paper still remembers how to bend.

bleedArticles.title: Every Listed Jumper Home
bleedArticles.body:
A supervised Jump into *Dracula* ended early on Sunday after Wicker Eddies wrote an unauthorized sentence in the source margin. The sentence read: *For one sentence, let him choose the verb.*

Professor Permancer opened the return. Every registered entrant answered the bookmark's check, and the Vault's roll was read twice. The source is closed while the annotation is examined.

Asked afterwards whether it was a prank, Eddies said, “I meant it.” He did not say what he'd meant. He was sitting on the Vault floor at the time with ink on his knee, and the Bleed noted that he did not look like a boy who was enjoying himself.

Penny Blackletter, who held the list, reports that all names were accounted for. The Bleed would like it on record that this was true when she said it.

Permancer has asked the Bleed to print the exact sentence. We have.

bleedArticles.title: Serenity Brown Awake
bleedArticles.body:
Serenity Brown is awake in the Kitchens after an attack in the East Stacks on Thursday. Count Dracula, who crossed out of his source during Sunday's return, deliberately used her to hold himself inside the Academy.

Brown can hear page-turns from books that are closed. She says it's like someone in the next room reading slowly. She's deciding what help she wants to give, and the Bleed has been asked to print that the deciding is hers. Reports go to Penny Blackletter. Visits go through Ambrose Trencher, who is strict about it and has put a ladle on the door.

No further injury has been reported. The East Stacks are closed to everyone, including the books.

Professor Permancer has confirmed that he opened the return invitation, and Wicker Eddies has confirmed his alteration to the source. Both are assisting with the investigation, and both have been seen carrying water.

bleedArticles.title: Several Places, One Entrance
bleedArticles.body:
A composite castle has grown through the East Stacks overnight. It's built, in order, of a library, a fortress, and a nursery. The Quillquarium drawbridge is real and closed to visitors. The nibs beneath it would like it noted that they didn't ask for this.

The nursery window belongs to a neighboring book. Please don't take it home.

Dracula's absence from his source is pulling other stories into the gap. A stair has opened between the supper tables. The soup is warm up there. Do not follow the soup.

The Academy has reconstructed the return conditions: an open source, an invitation the Count will recognize, and withdrawal of the living claim. The first two can be built. The third can't be built by anyone but the person who holds it.

Serenity Brown has agreed to the controlled return. The final condition is hers to release.

bleedArticles.title: The Count Returned
bleedArticles.body:
Dracula is back in *Dracula.* The borrowed rooms have gone home to their books, the stair is a stair in a story again, and the drawbridge has been returned to the Quillquarium's nibs with an apology and a quantity of ink.

Serenity Brown still hears the crossings. She has named the change Nightbound and asked the Bleed to print it. We're printing it. She was in the Kitchens this morning, complaining about her cards, which keep coming up moons.

The Vault's new return list names every permitted traveller and must be checked from both sides. Professor Permancer has suspended ordinary teaching Jumps while the safeguards are fitted, and has asked that the school be patient. The school will publish the reopening when it has one.

Wicker Eddies helped close the breach. The original annotation remains in the record, and so does the fact that he held the last fold.

bleedArticles.title: The Week, With Corrections
bleedArticles.body:
For anyone who missed it, and the Bleed has noticed that several readers did: a supervised Jump into *Dracula* ended early after Wicker Eddies wrote one unauthorized sentence in the source margin. Every listed jumper came home. Count Dracula had crossed out of his book during the return, and he used Serenity Brown to hold himself inside the Academy.

The East Stacks are shut. Serenity is awake in the Kitchens and can hear page-turns from closed books. She is choosing, one day at a time, who visits. Professor Permancer opened the return invitation, and Eddies altered the source. Both are helping with the investigation, and both have been asked to stop saying technically.

Ambrose is feeding everyone. The pear tart has been rationed. The Quillquarium still splashes uphill.

That is the entire weather.

bleedArticles.title: Two Weeks In, Briefly
bleedArticles.body:
The story so far: the Count is out of his book, the East Stacks are shut, and Serenity Brown is deciding what help she wants to give.

This week the Academy did paperwork, which is how it fights. Professor Villanelle put Wicker Eddies's sentence on the board, and nobody laughed. Permancer has been in the Vault since before breakfast. This reporter went round the back of the chalk door to see what's there. It has a back. Permancer followed. We both came out again, and neither of us will say what we saw.

The Count has been found in the Old Reading Room, reading his own book with a pencil. Serenity went in to speak to him. She came out and went directly to lunch.

Her map still moves when nobody touches it. It isn't subtle.

bleedArticles.title: Where Things Are Now
bleedArticles.body:
If one column gets read this week, make it this one. The Academy has company.

A composite castle has grown through the East Stacks, which remain shut. A drawbridge now crosses the Quillquarium. It's real, it's polite, and it's closed to visitors. A window from a neighboring book's nursery has appeared in a corridor. Please don't take it home. A stair has opened between the supper tables, going up to a hall nobody was invited to. The soup is warm up there. Do not follow the soup.

Sending everything home takes three things: the source, the invitation, and Serenity Brown's withdrawal of the living claim. Ambrose has proposed terms. Eddies has proposed a paper room, and been told to fix the window.

Serenity has agreed to the return. The last condition is hers.

bleedArticles.title: October, Corrected
bleedArticles.body:
The month, for the record. A Jump went wrong on a Sunday, the Count came out of his book, and the East Stacks shut. A composite castle, a drawbridge and a nursery window moved in. All of them are home now, and so is he.

Serenity Brown still hears the crossings. She has named the change Nightbound and asked us to print it. We have. Professor Permancer has pinned a return list to the Vault door and written on both sides of it, in case one side lies. Ordinary teaching Jumps are suspended while the safeguards are fitted.

Wicker Eddies helped close the breach. The annotation stays in the record: *For one sentence, let him choose the verb.* The Bleed has noticed that he has stopped looking at the Kitchens door when he walks past it. We're told this means something. We're not going to say what.

The tart has been restocked.
